dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: LocalDef001(M,P) is the conjunction of: every entry M(i,k) is nonnegative; and, for every real vector z and index i, sum_j M(i,j)(z(j) - sum_k P(j,k)z(k)) = z(i). Equivalently, M is entrywise nonnegative and M(I-P) acts exactly as the identity on every vector.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Applied to M1 and P, it supplies both the entrywise nonnegativity needed to preserve the componentwise correction inequality under multiplication by M1 and the exact identity M1(I-P)=I used to eliminate correction from the final bound.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a matrix A and vector x, LocalDef002(A,x,i) is the matrix-vector product component (Ax)(i) = sum over j in Fin n of A(i,j)x(j).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It defines every occurrence of P times correction, M1 times the componentwise absolute old residual, and M1 times data, as finite matrix-vector sums.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: LocalDef003(x) is the componentwise absolute-value vector, with LocalDef003(x)(i) = |x(i)|.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes LocalDef002(M1,LocalDef003(oldResidual),i) equal to sum_j M1(i,j)|oldResidual(j)|.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin
dependency_coverage.meaning: Fin n is the finite index type consisting of the n natural-number indices 0 through n-1.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It fixes all vectors to have n components and both matrices to have n rows and n columns.

dependency_coverage.name: HAdd.hAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: HAdd.hAdd selects the binary addition operation supplied by a heterogeneous-addition typeclass instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With the supplied real instance, all its occurrences are ordinary addition of real numbers.

dependency_coverage.name: HMul.hMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: HMul.hMul selects the binary multiplication operation supplied by a heterogeneous-multiplication typeclass instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With the supplied real instance, all its occurrences are ordinary multiplication of real numbers.

dependency_coverage.name: LE.le
dependency_coverage.meaning: LE.le selects the less-than-or-equal relation supplied by an LE typeclass instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With Real.instLE, it gives all componentwise inequalities their ordinary real-number ordering.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat
dependency_coverage.meaning: Nat is the type of natural numbers, including zero.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The dimension n is an arbitrary natural number and may therefore be zero.

dependency_coverage.name: OfNat.ofNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: OfNat.ofNat interprets a natural-number literal in a type using the corresponding OfNat instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets the displayed literals 1 and, indirectly through LocalDef001, 0 as real numbers.

dependency_coverage.name: One.toOfNat1
dependency_coverage.meaning: One.toOfNat1 constructs the interpretation of the literal 1 from a type's distinguished multiplicative-one element.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For Real, it ensures every expression 1 + us or 1 + u uses the real number one.

dependency_coverage.name: Real
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real is the type of real numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: All scalar parameters, matrix entries, vector entries, arithmetic expressions, absolute values, and inequalities are over the real numbers.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real.instAdd supplies ordinary real addition.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It determines the additions in all bounds, matrix-sum terms, and expressions such as 1 + us, 1 + u, and data(i) + (M1 data)(i).

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAddGroup
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real.instAddGroup supplies the standard additive-group structure on the reals, including additive inverses.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is one of the structures used to define real absolute value as max(a,-a).

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instLE
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real.instLE supplies the standard less-than-or-equal relation on the reals.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the nonnegativity condition on M1 and all assumed and concluded bounds ordinary real inequalities.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real.instMul supplies ordinary real multiplication.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It determines scalar products, matrix-vector summands, and the coefficient (1+us)(1+u)gammaR.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instOne
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real.instOne supplies the standard real multiplicative identity 1.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It gives the real constant in the factors 1 + us and 1 + u.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.lattice
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real.lattice supplies the standard lattice structure on the reals, including maximum.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supports the definition of each real absolute value appearing in the assumptions and conclusion.

dependency_coverage.name: abs
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a lattice-ordered additive group, abs(a) is max(a,-a); on the reals this is the usual absolute value |a|.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is applied to each selected component of oldResidual and newResidual and, through LocalDef003, componentwise to all of oldResidual before multiplication by M1.

dependency_coverage.name: instHAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: instHAdd promotes a homogeneous Add operation to a heterogeneous-addition instance by using that same addition.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Together with Real.instAdd, it makes each HAdd.hAdd in the declaration ordinary real addition.

dependency_coverage.name: instHMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: instHMul promotes a homogeneous Mul operation to a heterogeneous-multiplication instance by using that same multiplication.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Together with Real.instMul, it makes each HMul.hMul in the declaration ordinary real multiplication.

dependency_coverage.name: And
dependency_coverage.meaning: And(P,Q) is logical conjunction, requiring both propositions P and Q.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It requires both parts of LocalDef001: entrywise nonnegativity of M1 and the exact M1(I-P)=I identity.

dependency_coverage.name: Eq
dependency_coverage.meaning: Eq(a,b) is exact equality between two terms of the same type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It makes the resolvent-like identity in LocalDef001 an exact componentwise equality for every vector, not an approximation or inequality.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin.fintype
dependency_coverage.meaning: Fin.fintype(n) equips Fin n with a finite enumeration containing every index exactly once.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It permits matrix-vector products to sum over all n valid column indices.

dependency_coverage.name: Finset.sum
dependency_coverage.meaning: Finset.sum(s,f) is the finite additive sum of f(j) over all j in the finite set s.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It realizes each matrix-vector component as the finite sum of its row-entry-times-vector-entry products.

dependency_coverage.name: Finset.univ
dependency_coverage.meaning: Finset.univ is the finite set containing every element of a finite type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: In LocalDef002 it makes each sum range over every j in Fin n.

dependency_coverage.name: HSub.hSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: HSub.hSub selects the subtraction operation supplied by a heterogeneous-subtraction typeclass instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: In LocalDef001 it forms the real component z(k) - (Pz)(k).

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAddCommMonoid
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real.instAddCommMonoid supplies the standard commutative additive-monoid structure on the reals, including zero and associative, commutative addition.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the algebraic structure required to define the finite real sums in every matrix-vector product.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real.instSub supplies real subtraction, defined by a - b = a + (-b).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It determines the subtraction z(k) - (Pz)(k) in the exact identity imposed by LocalDef001.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instZero
dependency_coverage.meaning: Real.instZero supplies the real number zero.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the zero in the entrywise condition 0 <= M1(i,k) and the additive identity for real finite sums.

dependency_coverage.name: Zero.toOfNat0
dependency_coverage.meaning: Zero.toOfNat0 constructs the interpretation of the literal 0 from a type's distinguished zero element.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: For Real, it interprets the zero used in LocalDef001's nonnegativity condition.

dependency_coverage.name: instHSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: instHSub promotes a homogeneous Sub operation to a heterogeneous-subtraction instance by using that same subtraction.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Together with Real.instSub, it makes the subtraction inside LocalDef001 ordinary real subtraction.

binders: n is an arbitrary natural number.
us, u, and gammaR are arbitrary real numbers.
M1 and P are real n-by-n matrices, represented as functions Fin n -> Fin n -> Real.
oldResidual, data, update, correction, and newResidual are arbitrary real n-vectors, represented as functions Fin n -> Real.
The asserted conclusion is componentwise for every index i in Fin n.
hypotheses: M1 is entrywise nonnegative: M1(i,k) >= 0 for every i,k in Fin n.
M1 is an exact left inverse of I-P on all real n-vectors: for every vector z and index i, sum_j M1(i,j)(z(j) - sum_k P(j,k)z(k)) = z(i).
For every i, correction(i) <= (P correction)(i) + (1+us)|oldResidual(i)| + (1+us)(1+u)gammaR data(i).
For every i, |newResidual(i)| <= us|oldResidual(i)| + (1+us)(1+u)gammaR data(i) + correction(i) + u update(i).
conclusions: For every i in Fin n, |newResidual(i)| <= us|oldResidual(i)| + (1+us)(M1|oldResidual|)(i) + (1+us)(1+u)gammaR(data(i) + (M1 data)(i)) + u update(i).
mathematical_definitions: For any matrix A and vector x, (Ax)(i) means sum over j in Fin n of A(i,j)x(j).
The vector |oldResidual| is defined componentwise by |oldResidual|(j) = |oldResidual(j)|.
Thus (M1|oldResidual|)(i) = sum_j M1(i,j)|oldResidual(j)| and (M1 data)(i) = sum_j M1(i,j)data(j).
The repeated scalar coefficient is exactly (1+us)(1+u)gammaR.
The statement M1(I-P)=I abbreviates the explicitly quantified identity M1(z-Pz)=z for every real n-vector z.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For arbitrary dimension, real scalars, matrices, and vectors, assume that M1 is entrywise nonnegative and exactly satisfies M1(I-P)=I. Assume also a one-sided componentwise upper bound on correction in terms of P times correction, the absolute old residual, and data, together with a componentwise base bound on the absolute new residual. Then each absolute new-residual component is bounded by the original us-scaled absolute old-residual term, plus (1+us) times M1 applied to the componentwise absolute old residual, plus (1+us)(1+u)gammaR times the sum of the corresponding data component and the corresponding component of M1 applied to data, plus u times the corresponding update component.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The dimension n may be zero. Then Fin n is empty, all componentwise assumptions and conclusions are vacuous, and both universally indexed clauses of LocalDef001 hold vacuously.
No positivity or nonnegativity assumptions are imposed on us, u, gammaR, data, update, correction, oldResidual, newResidual, or P. Only M1 is required to be entrywise nonnegative.

Because the right-hand sides contain signed quantities and unrestricted scalar coefficients, they need not be nonnegative. In particular, the base hypothesis can be impossible at an index if its right-hand side is negative, making the overall implication vacuous for such data.
The condition M1(I-P)=I is exact and may itself be unsatisfiable for a given P; no approximate inverse or normwise resolvent condition is encoded.
The correction hypothesis is a one-sided bound on correction(i), not a bound on |correction(i)|.
Absolute values are applied only to oldResidual and newResidual. The data, update, correction, and matrix-vector product terms remain signed.
The result is a componentwise scalar inequality, not a vector-norm bound.

The vector names do not encode any recurrence or computational relationship. Apart from the stated inequalities, the proposition does not assert that newResidual, oldResidual, data, update, and correction arise from an algorithm.
There are no existentially quantified witnesses and no assertion that any of the hypotheses can be realized.
